rationale: Velosiraptor synthesizes verified low-level OS code for configuring memory translation and protection hardware. Its output is OS memory-management code and hardware components, not compute kernels for ML or accelerator workloads.

vAttention uses CUDA virtual memory management to keep the KV cache virtually contiguous while avoiding physical-memory fragmentation. The approach is a memory-management design that reuses existing attention kernels out of the box, so it is above-kernel rather than a new kernel-style optimization.

Virtuoso is a virtual-memory simulation framework with a lightweight userspace OS kernel for evaluating hardware/OS VM schemes. It improves research methodology and simulator accuracy rather than proposing compute kernels or kernel-level optimizations.

iTP+xPTP proposes cooperative STLB and L2 cache replacement policies to prioritize instruction translations and page-table data. These are microarchitectural replacement policies for caches/TLBs, not software kernels or compiler-generated kernels.

The paper characterizes pre-propagation GNNs and proposes optimized data loading schemes and tailored training methods to improve throughput. These are model-training/data-pipeline optimizations rather than kernel implementations or kernel-generation techniques.

SwiftVI is a suite of value-iteration algorithms for planning and learning with MDPs that prunes actions using priority queues and bounds. The contribution is algorithmic decision-process optimization, not kernel-level compute optimization.

The paper partitions vocabulary layers across pipeline devices and integrates vocabulary parallelism into pipeline schedules to balance computation and memory. This is a distributed training parallelization/scheduling strategy, which the codebook excludes when it does not generate or contribute kernels.

Youmu redesigns the data pipeline so LLM training can consume columnar data directly using page-level I/O and page-level shuffling. The optimization is storage/data loading for training, not a compute kernel or kernel compiler.

LeanAttention redesigns decode-phase attention execution and uses Stream-K-style partitioning to balance attention work across hardware, achieving speedups over FlashDecoding/FlashInfer. Attention is explicitly a kernel-style primitive in the codebook, and the stated contribution is an optimized attention execution mechanism.

Photon is a federated system for decentralized end-to-end LLM pre-training that reduces communication by combining local parallelism and low-bandwidth Local SGD. Its contributions are distributed training algorithms and system design, not kernel-level optimizations.

MEADOW proposes a token-parallel head-sequential dataflow and weight-packing execution strategy for LLMs on low-power FPGAs, reducing off-chip memory accesses and latency. This is a hardware-aware dataflow/layout mapping for LLM computation on an existing FPGA platform, so it fits kernel-style scheduling/layout optimization.

The paper reviews and empirically evaluates existing KV-cache compression techniques and provides tools/measurement guidance for production serving. It does not propose a new precision format implementation, kernel, or kernel-support mechanism itself.
